description: A hand-drawn clientside atlas for roleplay servers - territories, roads, quill inscriptions, dated marks, and maps you sign and hand to other players. A fork of Antique Atlas 4 for Minecraft 1.21.8.

releases.notes:
Inscriptions you can letter across the land yourself, the way territory names are written.

- **New: lettered inscriptions.** An inscription can now be written in large spaced capitals instead of on a plate, the same hand as a territory name, but with no zone attached. Switch *Style* in the inscription's dialog between plain and curved; a new inscription starts in whichever style you used last.
- **Bend it by three points.** Lettered inscriptions and territory names get a *Bend* box in their dialog: the name drawn along its curve, with a handle at the start, the middle and the end. Drag any of them up or down; right-click puts the default arch back. A territory you never bend keeps arching itself to fit its land, as before.
- **Turn, size and when it shows.** Together with the turn that was already there, inscriptions and territory names now have a size, and a range of zooms they show at: *Shown from* and *Shown up to* read the same as the scale bookmark (8b, 1c, 4c…), and either end can be left open. Lettering grows and shrinks with the map by default, like the land it names; *Grows with map* pins it to one size on screen instead. Plates keep one size, as they always have.
- Inscriptions are now picked by their writing: hovering or clicking anywhere on the letters finds them, however far they are turned or bent.

Inscriptions and territories already on your map look exactly as they did: plates keep their size, inscriptions still fade out past 4c, and territory names keep their automatic arch.

mods.description: A hand-drawn atlas for roleplay servers: territories, roads, quill inscriptions, dated marks, and maps you sign and share.

releases.notes:
Travelling by map, marks brought over from Xaero's, and a dialog that fits the screen it is on.

- **New: travel by map, where the game allows it.** Ctrl-click a mark, a bookmark or any spot on the map and the atlas sends you there, reading the height off the survey so a hillside lands on the hillside. It is offered only where the server actually lets you run the command – the atlas asks the command list the server sent your client, so nothing is promised that the server would refuse. Servers that hand travel out through a plugin, or under another name, are covered by two settings under Marks: whether it is offered at all, and what command to send.
- **New: bring your waypoints over from Xaero's.** Under Import/Export maps, the import side now reads Xaero's minimap waypoints as well as our own scrolls: pick the world, tick the sets to take, and they come in as marks with their names, heights and colours. Xaero's sets become layers of the same name, unless you would rather have everything in your personal layer. The land itself is not carried over – Xaero records neither the survey nor the structures the atlas draws from, so the map still fills in as you walk it.
- **Fixed: the mark dialog no longer covers its own buttons.** At a large GUI scale the dialog was taller than the screen, and "Готово" and "Отмена" ended up hidden behind the note box. The dialog is now laid out for the height it actually has: it tightens up when it must, and if even that is not enough the middle scrolls while the title and the confirm row stay put.

Settings and saved atlases carry over untouched.

releases.notes:
Minecraft **1.21.8**.

Fixes and map-label controls, shaped by the release server's feedback.

- **Fixed: a held drawing tool machine-gunned buttons.** Holding the left mouse button and moving the cursor re-fired whatever was under it many times a second, with the click sound stuttering along. A drag is now a drag: it no longer falls through to a click, so buttons fire once and sliders drag smoothly.
- **Turn a label, drop its shadow.** Territory names and pen inscriptions can be spun to any angle, and their shadow turned off, from the mark's own dialog. Routes get the shadow control too – for them it hides the dark ribbon behind the name, leaving it as bare ink along the path.
- **Fixed: the zone radius did nothing on territories.** A territory's place-name title only fired when you stood on the claim, ignoring the radius slider. The radius now works: the title announces the place as you come within that distance of its edge, not only once you are inside it.
- **New: how long a place name holds.** A setting under Place names sets how many seconds a zone title stays on screen before it fades.
- **New: resize the atlas in your hands.** A setting under The map scales the held book, and two rebindable keys (unbound by default) enlarge and shrink it on the fly.
- **Fixed: the dialog buttons could be cut off.** At a high GUI scale the marker dialog ran off the bottom of the screen and "Готово" / "Изменить границы" went with it. The bottom row now stays on screen instead of being pushed off.
- **The global zone radius left the settings.** It only duplicated the radius each named mark already carries and set them apart, so it is gone – the radius lives on the mark, where you set it. Marks with no radius of their own use the usual 32 blocks.
- **New: a zone-title cooldown.** A setting under Place names can hold the same place from announcing itself again for a while, so a title no longer flickers when you step across its edge and back. Off by default – titles appear at once, as before; raise it to add the delay.

Settings and saved atlases carry over untouched.
